solution: An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its two remote interior angles. Here \(\angle ACD\) is the exterior angle at C, and its remote interior angles are \(\angle A\) and \(\angle B\). So \(\angle ACD = \angle A + \angle B = 70^\circ + 40^\circ\). Hence \(\angle ACD = 110^\circ\).

The sum of the measures of the angles of a triangle is \(180^\circ\). So \(\angle P + \angle Q + \angle R = 180^\circ\), that is \(70^\circ + 65^\circ + \angle R = 180^\circ\), which gives \(\angle R = 180^\circ - 135^\circ\). Hence \(\angle R = 45^\circ\).

The measures of the angles of a triangle add up to \(180^\circ\), so \(x + (x - 20) + (x - 40) = 180\). Then \(3x - 60 = 180\), so \(3x = 240\) and \(x = 80\). The three measures are \(x^\circ = 80^\circ\), \((x - 20)^\circ = 60^\circ\) and \((x - 40)^\circ = 40^\circ\). Hence the angles measure \(80^\circ\), \(60^\circ\) and \(40^\circ\).

Let the smallest angle measure \(x^\circ\). Then the other two measure \(2x^\circ\) and \(3x^\circ\). Their sum is \(180^\circ\), so \(x + 2x + 3x = 180\), that is \(6x = 180\) and \(x = 30\). Hence the three angles measure \(30^\circ\), \(60^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\).

Since T - E - M, ray ET and ray EM are opposite rays, so \(\angle TEN\) and \(y\) form a linear pair. Hence \(y = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ\).
Since N - M - R, ray MN and ray MR are opposite rays, so \(\angle EMR\) and \(z\) form a linear pair. Hence \(z = 180^\circ - 140^\circ = 40^\circ\).
The angles of \(\triangle NEM\) add to \(180^\circ\), so \(x = 180^\circ - y - z = 180^\circ - 80^\circ - 40^\circ = 60^\circ\).
As a check, \(\angle EMR\) is an exterior angle of \(\triangle NEM\) at M, and \(x + y = 60^\circ + 80^\circ = 140^\circ\) as required.
Hence \(x = 60^\circ\), \(y = 80^\circ\) and \(z = 40^\circ\).

Line AB \(\parallel\) line DE and line AD is a transversal, so \(\angle BAD\) and \(\angle ADE\) are alternate angles. Hence \(\angle ADE = \angle BAD = 70^\circ\), that is \(\angle RDE = 70^\circ\).
In \(\triangle DRE\) the angles add to \(180^\circ\), so \(\angle DRE = 180^\circ - \angle RDE - \angle DER = 180^\circ - 70^\circ - 40^\circ = 70^\circ\).
Since A - R - D, ray RA and ray RD are opposite rays, so \(\angle ARE\) and \(\angle DRE\) form a linear pair, giving \(\angle ARE = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\).
Hence \(\angle DRE = 70^\circ\) and \(\angle ARE = 110^\circ\).

In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A + \angle B = 180^\circ - \angle C = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\).
Ray AO bisects \(\angle A\) and ray BO bisects \(\angle B\), so \(\angle OAB = \frac{1}{2}\angle A\) and \(\angle OBA = \frac{1}{2}\angle B\). Adding, \(\angle OAB + \angle OBA = \frac{1}{2}(\angle A + \angle B) = \frac{1}{2} \times 110^\circ = 55^\circ\).
In \(\triangle AOB\) the angles add to \(180^\circ\), so \(\angle AOB = 180^\circ - 55^\circ\).
Hence \(\angle AOB = 125^\circ\).

Line AB \(\parallel\) line CD and line PQ is the transversal, so \(\angle BPQ\) and \(\angle PQD\) are interior angles on the same side of the transversal. Therefore \(\angle BPQ + \angle PQD = 180^\circ\).
Ray PT bisects \(\angle BPQ\), so \(\angle TPQ = \frac{1}{2}\angle BPQ\). Ray QT bisects \(\angle PQD\), so \(\angle TQP = \frac{1}{2}\angle PQD\).
Adding these, \(\angle TPQ + \angle TQP = \frac{1}{2}(\angle BPQ + \angle PQD) = \frac{1}{2} \times 180^\circ = 90^\circ\).
In \(\triangle PTQ\) the three angles add to \(180^\circ\), so \(m\angle PTQ = 180^\circ - (\angle TPQ + \angle TQP) = 180^\circ - 90^\circ\).
Hence \(m\angle PTQ = 90^\circ\).

\(\angle b\) and the given angle of \(70^\circ\) are vertically opposite angles, so \(\angle b = 70^\circ\).
\(\angle c\) and the given angle of \(100^\circ\) lie on the base line and form a linear pair, so \(\angle c = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ\).
The angles of the triangle add to \(180^\circ\), so \(\angle a = 180^\circ - 70^\circ - 80^\circ = 30^\circ\).
As a check, the \(100^\circ\) angle is an exterior angle of the triangle and \(\angle a + \angle b = 30^\circ + 70^\circ = 100^\circ\).
Hence \(\angle a = 30^\circ\), \(\angle b = 70^\circ\) and \(\angle c = 80^\circ\).

Since E - F - M, \(\angle DFM\) is an exterior angle of \(\triangle DEF\) at F, so \(\angle DFM = \angle DEF + \angle EDF\).
Line DE \(\parallel\) line GF and line EM is a transversal, so \(\angle DEF\) and \(\angle GFM\) are corresponding angles, giving \(\angle GFM = \angle DEF\).
Ray FG bisects \(\angle DFM\), so \(\angle GFM = \frac{1}{2}\angle DFM = \frac{1}{2}(\angle DEF + \angle EDF)\).
Equating the two expressions for \(\angle GFM\), \(\frac{1}{2}(\angle DEF + \angle EDF) = \angle DEF\), so \(\angle DEF + \angle EDF = 2\angle DEF\) and therefore \(\angle EDF = \angle DEF\).
(i) Ray EG bisects \(\angle DEF\), so \(\angle DEG = \frac{1}{2}\angle DEF\). Since \(\angle DEF = \angle EDF\), this gives \(\angle DEG = \frac{1}{2}\angle EDF\).
(ii) Line DE \(\parallel\) line GF and line EG is a transversal, so \(\angle DEG\) and \(\angle EGF\) are alternate angles, giving \(\angle EGF = \angle DEG\). Also ray EG bisects \(\angle DEF\), so \(\angle GEF = \frac{1}{2}\angle DEF = \angle DEG\). Therefore \(\angle GEF = \angle EGF\).
In \(\triangle EFG\) the sides opposite congruent angles are congruent; the side opposite \(\angle GEF\) is FG and the side opposite \(\angle EGF\) is EF. Hence EF = FG.
